task.description: Full fresh security review of commit 77c1d1e against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8. In addition to re-confirming your prior findings still hold (per-version capability isolation, checkout immutability, ref-count manipulation resistance, Process.monitor/:DOWN correctness, no guest input reaching Letflow.Repo, supervision wiring), specifically verify the NEW registration-time capability-aware proof: (1) confirm the proof instance is GenServer.stop'd on EVERY path where a pid was produced, with no leak; (2) confirm the proof's import table is built from the CALLER-SUPPLIED manifest passed to register_version/3, never from any other module's or version's manifest, so a proof for module A's registration cannot accidentally validate against module B's capability grant; (3) confirm this new proof mechanism cannot be used to probe/fingerprint whether a given capability would be granted without actually registering a version (i.e. it's not exploitable as an oracle) -- if it can be, assess whether that's a real risk or an accepted, non-guest-reachable internal API surface; (4) confirm switching the data model to raw bytes doesn't introduce any new place where guest-supplied or otherwise untrusted bytes flow into a Repo call or similar tenant-scoped resource.
acceptance_criteria: a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
a module requiring at least one host capability can be successfully registered via register_version/3 -- verified by the actual test passing, not merely asserted
